name: AI Litigation
blurb: Living case pages for AI lawsuits in United States courts, refreshed from the dockets daily.

reading.body:
AI litigation in United States courts is tracked daily across claim families from copyright to government contracts, and current defenses lean on a small set of precedents decided before generative models existed.

The tracker labels every case by claim family, including copyright, right of publicity, product liability and wrongful death, hiring discrimination, biometric privacy, securities fraud, trade secrets, platform access, patent, consumer protection, and government contracts. Docket timelines refresh daily from CourtListener, so the record of motions and rulings stays current rather than frozen at filing.

The companion case law resource profiles the older decisions AI defendants actually cite: Sony on substantial non-infringing use, Campbell and Google Books on transformative purpose, Van Buren and hiQ on scraping, and Zeran on Section 230. Each profile states what the case held, why AI defendants cite it, and where the analogy is weakest, with a link to the opinion.

This data covers litigation only. It says nothing about compute, buildings, or power, and it does not measure how these cases affect model training or deployment costs.
